rows.name: Amazon S3 events + AWS Lambda standard function (Managed Instances 제외)
rows.reason: Standard Lambda stops after 15 minutes, preventing direct hour-long execution; S3 events are delivered at least once and need separate deduplication.

rows.name: Celery 4.2 with a RabbitMQ broker
rows.reason: Celery 4.2/RabbitMQ provides distributed workers, routing and acknowledgment controls, not admission deduplication. Durable admission/idempotent effects remain necessary; early acknowledgment risks loss, late acknowledgment permits retries; worker-loss semantics need configuration.

rows.name: pg-boss
rows.reason: PostgreSQL SKIP LOCKED claims through Node.js queue APIs reduce custom plumbing. Claims do not guarantee logical registration/external-effect deduplication; current deduplication and long-job options require verification.

rows.name: CS Browser (formerly S3 Browser)
rows.reason: CS Browser manages S3 buckets/objects through transfers, synchronization and administration, not job-executing worker distribution. Exclusion concerns documented operating scope; missing deduplication claims remain unknown rather than unsupported.

rows.name: Slurm
rows.reason: Provides batch scheduling, resource allocation, and job arrays with concurrency limits for many long tasks; registration deduplication and safe requeue handling remain application responsibilities.

rows.name: Amazon S3 events + AWS Lambda standard function (Managed Instances 제외)
rows.reason: Standard Lambda's 15-minute limit conflicts with hour-long tasks. Managed Instances' 90-minute exception is excluded; splitting jobs or dispatch-only use changes the proposed execution configuration.

rows.name: Celery Once (QueueOnce)
rows.reason: Celery Once rejects equivalent pending/running tasks with submission locks. Default one-hour locks can expire across queue/run time; direct calls/retries need review. Locks are not permanent completion deduplication.

rows.name: Slurm
rows.reason: Cluster scheduling fits; singleton only serializes, no-requeue may be overridden. Durable admission deduplication, enforced restart policy, one-hour partitions and capacity unverified. Optional requeue alone does not justify exclusion.

rows.name: Amazon SQS FIFO queues
rows.reason: FIFO deduplication IDs and visibility leases provide admission deduplication and worker claims. Producer deduplication is time-bounded; expired visibility or crashes before deletion permit repeats. Preserve a durable result ledger.

rows.name: Bull job IDs and renewable job locks
rows.reason: Bull rejects existing jobIds and uses renewable Redis locks. Stalled recovery can repeat processing; deletion removes retained identity, and CPU-bound handlers can disrupt lock renewal.

rows.name: pg-boss
rows.reason: Node.js/PostgreSQL claims/atomic commits with automatic retries do not prove nonrepeating task execution despite exactly-once search snippet. Release-specific deduplication/retry/expiry and exact timeout configuration unverified.

rows.name: PostgreSQL job ledger with unique task keys and atomic permanent claims
rows.reason: PostgreSQL separates durable admission deduplication from permanent worker claims. Strict at-most-once starts prohibit retrying uncertain claims, potentially stranding work. Task identity and acceptable failure recovery still require confirmation.

rows.name: PostgreSQL unique job ledger with ON CONFLICT and FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
rows.reason: PostgreSQL unique keys reject duplicate jobs; transactional SKIP LOCKED distributes claims. Short transactions require leases/recovery; external effects need idempotency/shared transactions, and stale workers must not commit after ownership loss.

rows.name: Celery 4.2.1 with early acknowledgment and an application-level identity ledger
rows.reason: Celery 4.2.1 early acknowledgment requires admission deduplication/invocation gating and can lose unfinished work. Retries/late acknowledgment undermine literal no-repeat claims. Broker/publish uncertainty, long-task limits and worker gating unverified.

rows.name: CS Browser (formerly S3 Browser)
rows.reason: Windows S3 file management and transfer software does not provide a distributed scheduler or deduplicated execution for arbitrary tasks lasting up to an hour.
